current.text: Nic Claxton is gone from Brooklyn, and Sharpe is the projected starting center.
The expert expects about 24 minutes a night. He doubts Sharpe reaches 28 minutes and says 30 is almost certainly not happening.
Sharpe has said he wants to double his minutes.

His rank depends on minutes, and the experts differ on how many he needs. One take says 24 minutes makes him about top 100 and 27 minutes about top 70. Another says 28 minutes as the center would lock him into the top 100.
Brooklyn signed Mo Wagner. The bench also has Danny Wolf and Noah Clowney, so three backup bigs compete for frontcourt minutes.
Wagner's signing lowers Sharpe's upside. Center minutes could become a messy split with Wagner and Wolf.
When Claxton missed games in the past, Sharpe sometimes still played very few minutes. He is on a short two-year deal.
The experts see him as underpriced in category leagues and a top 100 player. He is one expert's best category-league target. His ESPN rank near 136 and a Fantrax ADP near 101 are called a bargain.
In an expert auction mock he went for 10 USD as a starting center. The buyer said that was still under his value.
A Yahoo rank in the high 80s is fair in category leagues. If he loses minutes, a pick at that rank becomes a bad one.
If he does not start early in the season, react right away.
Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins. It does not own its draft pick, so it has no reason to tank.
Brooklyn's March minutes are uncertain. The team has no team-building reason to win beyond player development, and it may experiment.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. With a March 28 end, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3 games (10 total) with one back-to-back.

durable.text: By the numbers he is one of the best offensive rebounders in the league. He has improved as a finisher and has become a versatile defender.
He used to be a shot blocker. His block rate has fallen while his passing and steals have gone up.
He is a per-minute monster who has rarely had the chance to start, so he does not need big minutes to be useful.
His category profile is built on rebounds, FG% and steals, and his steals are high for a center. He makes almost no threes, and his FT% is below the pool.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
Plain nine-cat rankings will inflate him to look like a much better player than he is.

note: Sharpe costs almost nothing on the market: 2.5 USD on Yahoo and 1 USD on ESPN, and nobody drafted him in our league last season. An expert still paid 10 USD in a mock auction and called that under value. Spending about 5 to 8 USD is reasonable for a starting center who gives rebounds (9.1 projected), FG% and steals that are high for a center. His mild FT% hit and lack of threes fit punt FT% or punt 3PM builds, although he is not flagged as a punt fit. In the first two weeks, check that he starts and plays 24 or more minutes ahead of Wagner and Wolf. If he does not, cut ties quickly.
